{"completeness":0.75,"citation_quality":0.65,"severity_defensibility":0.72,"overall_pass":true,"feedback":"The investigation demonstrates good foundational analysis with appropriate severity assessment and response recommendations, but has notable gaps that should be addressed in future triages. First, the ATT&CK technique citations need better justification—T1048 and T1052.001 are cited but the alert shows a blocked read attempt with no evidence of actual exfiltration occurring or the specific protocols/channels involved; T1005 is more defensible given the attempted file access. Second, the analysis conflates the EDR block reason ('data_exfiltration_prevention') with confirmed malware presence, but the alert only indicates a blocked access attempt—there's no explicit confirmation that malware was actually running on the system versus suspicious process behavior triggering the rule. Third, identity signals were appropriately marked as 'None,' but the analysis could have noted the cross-user access attempt (erodriguez accessing Administrator files) as a key suspicious indicator worth investigating further. Finally, while the response recommendations are thorough and appropriate for a suspected compromise, the investigation should have flagged the need to verify whether the block actually prevented data staging or if no data was accessed at all, which would inform containment priority. These refinements will strengthen future triage submissions."}
